definitions.explanation: Describes light or small objects appearing and disappearing repeatedly in an unstable, intermittent way.
Looking at something repeatedly but briefly, often in a furtive manner.
Falling or appearing in small, sparse amounts (like light snow).

examples.japanese: {星|ほし}がちらちら{光|ひか}っている。
ろうそくの{火|ひ}がちらちら{揺|ゆ}れている。
{木|き}の{葉|は}の{間|あいだ}から{日|ひ}の{光|ひかり}がちらちら{見|み}えた。
examples.english: Sunlight flickered through the gaps in the leaves.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{彼|かれ}のことをちらちら{見|み}ていた。
examples.english: She kept stealing glances at him.

examples.japanese: {授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう}、{隣|となり}の{席|せき}の{子|こ}がちらちらこちらを{見|み}てきた。
examples.english: During class, the kid in the next seat kept glancing my way.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}がちらちら{降|ふ}ってきた。
{桜|さくら}の{花|はな}びらがちらちら{散|ち}っている。
examples.english: Cherry blossom petals are drifting down in small flurries.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}からちらちら{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}っていたが、{午後|ごご}には{止|や}んだ。
examples.english: Light snow was falling since morning, but it stopped in the afternoon.

notes:
ONOMATOPOEIA TYPE:
Giseigo/gitaigo - mimetic word expressing manner of action.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・ちらちら{光|ひか}る - to flicker/twinkle
・ちらちら{見|み}る - to steal glances
・{雪|ゆき}がちらちら{降|ふ}る - snow falls in light flurries
・ちらちら{見|み}える - to be barely visible, to catch glimpses of

RELATED MIMETICS:
・きらきら - sparkling, glittering (more steady, beautiful light)
・ぴかぴか - shiny, gleaming (solid brightness)
・じろじろ - staring (prolonged, often rude)

NUANCE:
ちらちら suggests intermittent, unstable, or furtive action - not continuous or steady.

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
